skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

version.changelog:
- Increased requirement evidence from 9 to 12 online signals, reflecting broader user demand.
- Updated demand and evidence details in skill documentation (SKILL.md and related files).
- Removed the redundant skill-card.md file.
- Improved clarity and alignment in all documentation (README, SKILL, and requirement plan files) for both English and Chinese audiences.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with broad activation wording but no code execution, data access, persistence, or deception.

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown/YAML guidance only and does not request network access, credentials, local indexing, external APIs, or privileged environment access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, scripts, dependencies, or executable setup are present; the only notable install-time behavior is agent metadata allowing implicit invocation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger metadata and examples use very broad words such as security, every, must, pass, and before, with implicit invocation enabled, so it may activate more often than users expect.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background process, memory writing, service registration, privilege escalation, or tool wrapping was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill provides procedural help for SkillScan-style workflow hardening, bug fixing, checklists, analysis, and implementation support, which matches its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: This skill appears safe to install as a workflow helper. Users should be aware that its activation phrases are broad, so they may want to invoke it explicitly only when they need SkillScan-style workflow or security-checklist help.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The overbroad trigger concern is supported by artifact text, especially the generic keyword lists and allow_implicit_invocation setting, but the underlying skill instructions are limited to benign workflow guidance and do not add high-impact authority.
[SQP-3] expected: The bilingual packaging and mixed English/Chinese wording are visible in the artifacts; this is a usability/localization issue rather than a security concern.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The supplied static scan reported no results, which is consistent with the absence of executable code, persistence, exfiltration, or privilege-seeking behavior in the inspected files.
